what_varies: The multiplier each side of the pan carries, with the term that is added after it taken off. That is not what a broadband sweep of this byte measures and this must not be scored against one: a broadband reading has the two together, and the whole of what this table says about the ends is that such a reading is reading the other one there. What it predicts is the band record, where the two are separable.
why_it_is_a_readout: One entry per setting is one free number per measurement, so it cannot come out wrong and it stays out of every ranking. What is worth having is not that it fits. It is that the entry is one number and not one per band: the same multiplier accounts for twenty bands of the take at once, over 342 readings to a median of 0.17 decibels, which is the thing a table read off a broadband sweep could not have shown.
recovered_up_to: A constant. Adding the same number to every entry and taking that number times the source off every floor leaves every figure in the record where it was, so the table is pinned by putting its quietest entry at silence, which is the end of that trade with the largest floor. The floor cannot be negative, which bounds the constant from above and so bounds the last entry's depth from one side only: it is at least 300 decibels under the first and nothing here says it is not silence.
